newsitem.title: TURKEY: Up to 11 die in Turkish prison riot.
newsitem.headline: Up to 11 die in Turkish prison riot.

text.p: Up to 11 people died and several were injured in a riot by rebel Kurds over prison conditions at Diyarbakir high-security jail, hospital officials said on Wednesday.
"We know the identity of eight of the dead, and we are trying to identify the other three," a Diyarbakir hospital official told reporters.
Justice minister Sevket Kazan said nine prisoners had died, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported. Kazan said he would make a fuller statement later.
Eight Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) inmates were reported dead late on Tuesday before security forces brought the unrest under control.

Turkey has focused much of its attention for the last three weeks on trying to stem any knock-on effects that the upheaval in neighbouring Iraq's Kurdish region might have on Turkey's own restive Kurds.
But highlighting the extent of separatist strife on Turkish soil, government troops this week launched big offensives against PKK rebels in the mountains of eastern Tunceli province.

In Diyarbakir on Wednesday, witnesses said security forces had barred entry and exit from the hospitals and prison. The prisoners' relatives crowded outside the hospital, chanting and making victory signs. Occasionally there were skirmishes between inmates' families and the police.

The hospital official said around 10 people were injured in the incident, sparked by a prisoner protest against the government's failure to improve prison conditions after a nationwide hunger strike in July.
The pro-PKK DEM news agency said 20 people were hurt.

"Soldiers and police mounted an attack against the PKK prisoners of war," the agency said in a statement. DEM quoted hospital sources as saying many of the dead and injured had wounds from bullets, makeshift skewers and wooden beams.
More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1984 in clashes between government forces and the rebels in a bitter fight that costs Turkey an estimated $8 billion annually.
